title: Robots directives overview
learningObjectives: Explain robots directives overview and choose appropriate document or embedded-resource metadata.

understand.concept: Robots directives communicate crawling or indexing preferences. They can be expressed through meta name=robots or HTTP headers such as X-Robots-Tag. Directives such as noindex affect indexing when processed by a crawler; robots.txt controls crawling access and is not a reliable way to keep private content secure.
understand.whyItMatters: Do not use robots directives as access control. Private or sensitive content must be protected by authentication and server-side authorization. A crawler cannot be forced to respect every directive.
understand.analogy: Robots directives are instructions for cooperative crawlers, not a lock on a private room.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy is simplified; metadata and embedding behaviour follow browser, HTTP, and search-engine processing rules.

explain.narrative: The meta directive asks compliant crawlers not to index the page while allowing link discovery. It does not prevent visitors from opening the URL.

examples.explanation: The meta directive asks compliant crawlers not to index the page while allowing link discovery. It does not prevent visitors from opening the URL.
examples.expectedOutput: A browser-rendered or document-head example demonstrating the HTML feature.

practise.guidedTask: Explain the difference between noindex, robots.txt disallow, and authentication. Identify which one actually protects private content.
practise.independentTask: Prepare a document head or embed example. Check accessibility, security permissions, and whether metadata accurately describes the content.
hints: Use absolute canonical URLs when declaring a canonical target.
Never treat crawler directives as access control.
Use restrictive iframe permissions and a meaningful title.

practice.starterCode:
<!doctype html>
<html lang="en"><head><meta charset="utf-8"><meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1"><title>Robots directives overview</title></head><body>
<head><meta name='robots' content='noindex,follow'></head>
</body></html>
practice.resetCode:
<!doctype html>
<html lang="en"><head><meta charset="utf-8"><meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1"><title>Robots directives overview</title></head><body>
<head><meta name='robots' content='noindex,follow'></head>
</body></html>

questions.prompt: Can robots.txt or noindex protect confidential information from public access?
questions.explanation: Crawling and indexing directives are not security controls; private content needs authorization.

questions.prompt: Which principle should guide metadata and embedding?
options: Accurate description, least privilege, and no false security assumptions
Use metadata as a substitute for authentication
Grant every embedded document all permissions
questions.answer: Accurate description, least privilege, and no false security assumptions
questions.explanation: Metadata should be accurate and embedded resources should receive only necessary capabilities.
